title: Open-image criterion for the universal surjectivity locus
statement: Let $S,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $p:X\to S$, $q:Y\to S$ and $f:X\to Y$ be morphisms with $q\circ f=p$. Suppose the topological image $I=f(|X|)\subseteq |Y|$ is open, and suppose $q$ is a closed map on underlying topological spaces, meaning that $q(D)$ is closed in $|S|$ whenever $D$ is closed in $|Y|$. Put $V=|S|\setminus q(|Y|\setminus I)$. Then $V$ is open and defines an open subscheme $V\hookrightarrow S$ with the restricted structure sheaf [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every scheme $T$ and morphism $h:T\to S$, the induced map $f_T:X\times_ST\to Y\times_ST$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] if and only if $h$ factors through $V\hookrightarrow S$.

source.place: Tag 05XC, spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-where-surjective-flat, proof from the displayed complement formula through the final point-lifting argument, specialized to schemes. This isolates the open-image argument: its hypotheses are openness of the image and closedness of q, without the earlier flatness hypotheses.

proof.text: Put $D=|Y|\setminus I$. Since $I$ is open, $D$ is closed, so the hypothesis on $q$ makes $q(D)$ closed. Its complement $V$ is open. Give $V$ the restricted structure sheaf. For every $v\in V$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] supplies an affine open neighbourhood $v\in U\subseteq V$ in $S$. On this neighbourhood the restricted sheaf is $\mathcal O_S|_U$, so $V$ is locally affine and hence a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Its inclusion $j:V\hookrightarrow S$ is an open immersion by [def-weil-open-immersion].

proof.text: Fix any scheme $T$ and $h:T\to S$. Write $a:X_T\to X$, $b:X_T\to T$, $r:Y_T\to Y$ and $s:Y_T\to T$ for the fibre-product projections. The induced $f_T$ satisfies $r f_T=f a$ and $s f_T=b$. The square with edges $a,f_T,f,r$ is cartesian: a test pair $u:W\to X$, $v:W\to Y_T$ with $fu=rv$ satisfies $pu=qfu=qrv=hsv$, so the pair $(u,sv)$ gives a unique $w:W\to X_T$. The maps $f_Tw$ and $v$ have equal projections $fu=rv$ and $sv$, hence agree. Uniqueness follows from the projections $a,b$. This proves the square's universal property using only [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 05XC, spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-where-surjective-flat, proof from the displayed complement formula through the final point-lifting argument, specialized to schemes. This isolates the open-image argument: its hypotheses are openness of the image and closedness of q, without the earlier flatness hypotheses.; cartesian square: Tag 01S1 (morphisms-lemma-base-change-surjective), first paragraph of proof.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image] to the cartesian square of Step 2, with the subset equal to all of $|X|$. It gives $f_T(|X_T|)=r^{-1}(I)$. Thus $f_T$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] exactly when $r^{-1}(D)=\varnothing$. Apply the same node to the defining square $Y_T=Y\times_ST$ and the subset $D\subseteq|Y|$; it gives $s(r^{-1}(D))=h^{-1}(q(D))$. A set has empty image under a function if and only if it is empty: a member of a nonempty set supplies a member of its image. Consequently $f_T$ is surjective if and only if $h^{-1}(q(D))=\varnothing$, equivalently $h(|T|)\subseteq V$.

proof.text: If $h(|T|)\subseteq V$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] to $h:T\to S$ and the open subscheme from Step 1. It supplies $h':T\to V$ with $j h'=h$. Conversely any such factorization has image in $V$ because $j$ is its inclusion. Combine this equivalence with Step 3 to obtain the asserted universal property for every $T$ and $h$.
